correctness.rationale: Local strong odd constraints yield an if-and-only-if two-mode classification; hub class parity and proper cycle word give exact lower bounds, extended seed constructions attain them. Odd-order recurrence derives from the explicit signed 3-by-3 transfer trace. Inclusion-exclusion proves the exceptional five-rim count. The 4-color rim case is counted by an explicit bijection to closed walks of a 12-state weighted transfer matrix over a parity group algebra. Two independent finite verification paths agree and do not replace the all-order proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Necessary odd hub color-class parity also occurs in the wheel theorem, but the wheel requires all rim colors at distance at most two to differ. Gear rims only require neighboring colors distinct, and subdivision colors create a second uniform mode. The wheel values (and their optimum counts) cannot be specialized to obtain the gear congruence transition, the n=5 exceptional count, or the 12-state gear transfer trace.

originality.rationale: Searches of exact gear/Jahangir terminology and scientific comparisons with accessible full-source discussions of the originating 2024 strong odd-coloring papers and the 2026 wheel theorem produced no identical or stronger implication. Wheel and gear neighborhood structures differ, and a public gear mixed-resolving result concerns another graph invariant. This is a best-knowledge conclusion, not a uniqueness guarantee.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible specialized studies might already compute strong odd coloring of gear/Jahangir graphs or an equivalent subdivision family.

value.rationale: A standard, motivated graph family exhibits a nontrivial parity-dependent strong odd chromatic phase diagram with an isolated six-color exception, a global local-rigidity dichotomy, and exact labeled optimum counts for every size. This clarifies how subdivision changes a recently developed vertex-coloring invariant relative to known wheel values.
